rich_summary: At the climax of Yudhishthira’s great sacrifice, sages, kings, and Brahmanas gather in the inner enclosure, creating a scene likened to a divine assembly in Brahma’s heaven. The sage Narada observes the gathering and reflects on a cosmic secret: many of the warriors present are incarnations of gods destined to destroy one another on earth as part of Narayana’s plan. Recognizing Krishna as that divine presence living among men, Narada sits in awe. Following ritual custom, Bhishma instructs Yudhishthira to offer the first ceremonial Arghya—the highest honor—to the most worthy guest. Bhishma declares Krishna supreme among them, and Sahadeva presents the offering. Krishna accepts it, but the proud king Sisupala erupts in anger, denouncing the choice and publicly insulting both Bhishma and Yudhishthira, setting the stage for a major conflict.

highlight_spans.why: Opens with the grand assembly of sages and kings at Yudhishthira’s sacrifice, establishing the sacred and political significance of the moment.
Narada reflects on the divine plan and the incarnations of gods among the gathered warriors, giving the scene cosmic weight.
Bhishma explains the rule of offering Arghya and proposes honoring the foremost person present—triggering the central decision of the chapter.
Bhishma declares Krishna supreme among the assembly, comparing him to the sun among luminous bodies.
Sisupala begins his furious protest, openly insulting Krishna, Bhishma, and the Pandavas, igniting the dramatic conflict.

top_scenes.scene_text: A vast sacrificial hall filled with kings and radiant sages like stars in the sky while Narada watches thoughtfully among them.
Sahadeva presenting the ceremonial Arghya to Krishna as Bhishma proclaims his greatness while the gathered monarchs look on.
Sisupala rising angrily in the royal assembly, pointing accusingly toward Krishna while shocked kings and elders surround him.
